title: Author an eCTD section in-app with sample pre-fill and Health Canada review
walkthrough:
You start on a page headed "Your product dossiers", with a top bar branded "ANDS Studio". You click "New dossier +", which reveals a card with two fields: "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456") and "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"). The ID must follow a specific format — if it doesn't, an error appears: "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". You click "Create & open →" and land in Module 1 of a three-part workspace: a section tree on the left, a working panel in the center, and a status rail on the right. The top bar shows module tabs M1–M5 plus chips for "Application Viewer" and "Audit".

In the left tree, each section shows its number, title, a status glyph, and a badge reading "req" or "opt". Clicking a section loads the center panel: an eyebrow line like "Module 1 · Section 1.2.1", the section title, and a guidance box titled "What Health Canada needs here" with format notes (e.g. "Bilingual: EN + FR") and a link "Health Canada guidance ↗".

Below the guidance sits an action bar with tabs such as "⬆ Upload", "✦ Author in-app", and "⊘ Mark N/A". You choose "✦ Author in-app". (On AI-draftable sections a second toggle appears — "💬 Draft with AI" vs "✦ Sample & edit" — this flow uses the form path.) A note explains: "Pre-filled with a realistic sample from your dossier — edit every field to your product, then author. Fields marked sample are worked examples to replace." The form loads with labeled fields like "Sponsor company", "Regulatory contact", "Canadian Reference Product (brand)"; placeholder-example fields carry a small "sample" tag.

You edit the fields, then click a button labeled with the section name, e.g. "Author Cover Letter →" (it reads "Authoring…" while busy). The document is generated and appears as an attached file with size, an md5 checksum snippet, an "authored" marker, and a "Download" link. A review runs automatically; you can also press "Review vs Health Canada" at any time. The result panel starts "Health Canada review:" and either says "no blocking content gaps." or lists counts to fix and check, with each finding showing a message, a suggested edit, and an "HC guidance ↗" link.

The right rail tracks "required sections complete" per module and three gate flags — "Documents", "Fee", "Valid eCTD" — toward filing readiness.
